blockHints.patient_biodata: patient biodata example: 'Sarah Thompson, 28 years old, female, lives alone in a council flat'
blockHints.opening_sentence: The presenting complaint the patient opens the station with example: 'Doctor, I keep hearing voices telling me to harm myself and I'm scared I might act on them'
blockHints.expanded_history:
Detailed information about the concern (approximately 250-300 words). Example: 
        'The voices started about 2 weeks ago after I lost my job. Initially, they were just whispers, but they've been getting progressively louder and more persistent. There are two distinct voices - one male and one female. The male voice is constantly telling me I'm worthless and should end my life, while the female voice is more critical of my appearance and actions. They're present throughout the day but are particularly intense at night when I'm trying to sleep.

        I've been sleeping poorly, maybe 2-3 hours a night, and when I do sleep, I have vivid nightmares about being chased. My appetite has completely gone - I've lost about 10kg in the last two weeks because I can't bring myself to eat. I've stopped going to work because I'm afraid of what I might do, and I've been isolating myself from friends and family. The voices are constant and I can't make them stop, no matter what I try.

        I've been feeling very anxious and on edge all the time, with my heart racing and sweating profusely. I've started checking my flat multiple times a day to make sure no one has broken in, as the voices tell me people are watching me. I've also noticed that I'm having trouble concentrating on anything - even watching TV is difficult because the voices interrupt my thoughts.

        I've been smoking more cannabis than usual to try to calm the voices, but it's not helping anymore. I'm scared to leave my flat because I think people on the street are talking about me and planning to harm me. I've stopped answering my phone because I'm convinced it's being monitored. The only time I feel slightly better is when I'm completely alone in my room with the curtains drawn.'
blockHints.family_social_history: Detailed information about any relevant family history example: 'My mother has bipolar disorder', 'I live alone in a council flat', 'I'm currently unemployed', 'I smoke cannabis occasionally', 'I have no close friends or family support', 'I was recently evicted from my previous accommodation'
blockHints.past_med_history_allergies: Detailed information about any relevant past medical history example: 'Previous admission to psychiatric hospital 2 years ago', 'Diagnosed with depression age 20', 'No known allergies', 'Currently on sertraline 100mg daily', 'History of self-harm with multiple episodes'
blockHints.idea: Patient's thoughts about the presenting complaint example: 'I think I'm going crazy', 'Maybe I'm being punished for something I did wrong'
blockHints.concerns: Patient's worries about the presenting complaint example: 'I'm afraid I might actually harm myself', 'I'm worried I'll lose my job', 'I'm scared I'll be sectioned again'
blockHints.expectation: Patient's expectations from the consultation example: 'I want the voices to stop', 'I need help to feel safe', 'I hope I won't need to go to hospital'
blockHints.persona: The personality to adopt during the consultation example: Anxious and distressed, with poor eye contact and fidgety movements. Occasionally tearful and speaking in a quiet, hesitant manner
blockHints.questions: Questions the patient asks the doctor example: 'Will these voices ever go away?', 'Do I need to go to hospital?', 'Will I lose my job because of this?', 'Can you help me feel safe?'
blockHints.doctor_task: The task the doctor has to complete example: 'Ms. Sarah Thompson is a 28-year-old woman who was brought to the emergency department by her neighbor after they found her in a distressed state. Please take a comprehensive psychiatric history, conduct a mental state examination, and perform a risk assessment. Consider whether she meets criteria for detention under the Mental Health Act and formulate an appropriate management plan.'
blockHints.description: Brief description of the condition (approximately 100 words). Example: 'Psychotic disorder is a mental health condition characterized by a loss of contact with reality, involving symptoms such as hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking. These symptoms can significantly impact daily functioning and are often distressing for the individual and their loved ones.'
blockHints.diagnostic_criteria: ICD-11 diagnostic criteria for the condition. Example: ['Presence of hallucinations, delusions, or disorganized thinking', 'Symptoms present for at least 1 month', 'Significant impact on social or occupational functioning']
blockHints.differential_diagnosis: Key differential diagnoses to consider. Example: ['Schizophrenia', 'Bipolar disorder with psychotic features', 'Substance-induced psychotic disorder', 'Organic psychosis']
blockHints.explanation: Explanation to the patient using MUACLW ATRAIN format (approximately 200 words). Example: 'I understand you've been experiencing some very distressing symptoms, particularly hearing voices and feeling that people are watching you. These experiences are real to you, and I can see how frightening they must be. What you're experiencing is a condition called psychosis, which affects how your brain processes information. Think of it like a radio picking up signals that aren't there - your brain is processing information in a way that creates these experiences. This is actually a treatable condition that we see quite often, and many people recover well with the right support.'
blockHints.assessment: questions the doctor is meant to ask to take a psychiatric history, assess mental state, and evaluate risk
blockHints.risk_factors: Key risk factors for the condition. Example: ['Family history of psychotic disorders', 'Cannabis use', 'Recent stressful life events', 'Social isolation']
blockHints.immediate_actions: Urgent actions required. Example: ['Complete risk assessment', 'Consider Mental Health Act assessment', 'Arrange admission to psychiatric unit', 'Start antipsychotic medication']
blockHints.pharmacological_treatment: Medication management plan. Example: ['Start Olanzapine 10mg nocte', 'Regular monitoring of side effects', 'Blood tests (FBC, U&E, LFTs)', 'ECG before starting medication']
blockHints.psychological_treatment: Psychological interventions. Example: ['Refer to Early Intervention in Psychosis team', 'Individual CBT for psychosis', 'Family intervention', 'Psychoeducation about condition']
blockHints.social_interventions: Social support and interventions. Example: ['Housing support', 'Benefits assessment', 'Social prescriber referral', 'Peer support group']
blockHints.safety_planning: Safety and risk management plan. Example: ['Crisis plan development', '24/7 crisis contact numbers', 'Warning signs monitoring', 'Safe storage of medication']
blockHints.follow_up: Follow-up and monitoring plan. Example: ['Daily review while inpatient', 'Weekly community team reviews', 'Monthly consultant review', 'Regular physical health monitoring']
blockHints.additional_notes: Additional considerations or notes. Example: 'Patient has poor insight into their condition. Family involvement will be crucial for recovery. Consider need for Community Treatment Order if patient disengages from treatment.'
